newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse says stock split on schedule.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse says stock split on schedule.

text.p: The chairman of Westinghouse Electric Corp said Wednesday the company's anticipated stock split was proceeding as scheduled and should be completed by the end of the third quarter.

"Our estimated date (for completion) is the end of September," Michael Jordan, Westinghouse chairman, told shareholders during the company's annual meeting in Minneapolis. "Our major objective is obtaining a tax-free ruling for the shareholders from the Internal Revenue Service."

Westinghouse, currently based in Pittsburgh, will separate its industrial and media operations into separate companies with separate stocks. The media operations will relocate to New York and the industrial segments will remain in Pittsburgh.
Westinghouse analysts had been expecting the transaction to be finished by the end of the third quarter.
In other business at the meeting, shareholders voted down a proposed resolution to rescind the current shareholders rights plan that includes a poison pill provision.
About 60 percent of shareholders voted against the resolution.
The resolution had been proposed by the Central Pension Fund of the International Union of Operating Engineers and Participating Employers, a group that owns 86,600 shares.
The group did not have a representative at the meeting.
The current shareholder rights plan was adopted in December 1995 and keeps the poison pill provision in place for ten years.
